items.title: Aebersold Jamey — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But Wilson Curia, a piano player from Sao Paolo, asked me to come down and do ten days of clinics and stuff.

ctx.x: But the technology itself has also allowed us to do things that we never could imagine.

Let me mention something else, too. We’ve got a DVD, the one DVD that we made. A guy invited me years ago, in ’92 maybe... I’ve lost track of time. But Wilson Curia, a piano player from Sao Paolo, asked me to come down and do ten days of clinics and stuff. He said, “While you’re here, the people who are going to pay for your transportation would like to do DVD, a video.” I said, “Well, I’ve never done that before.” He said, “Well, they’d like for you to do it.” I said, “What if I don’t like the video?” He said,…

It’s one of the best things I ever did. They spliced it together. No help from me. I guess my piano player friend, Wilson Curia, helped them put it together. We sold a lot of them, and it’s been very, very helpful. I’ve had people write me an email and say, “Jamey, I spend time with you every day at lunch. I put the video in and I’m eating lunch with you. It’s so nice, because if I don’t understand something, I can back it up and play it again, play it again.” But it’s been very, very helpful, that DVD. It’s…
